extracted.intended_audience: Applicants submitting NDAs or ANDAs to FDA; regulatory affairs and legal professionals in the pharmaceutical industry
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and content/format standards for reporting ACNU failures, requesting waivers, submitting petitions, and preparing abbreviated new drug applications (ANDAs) under 21 CFR Part 314. Covers required dataset elements, timing, format, recordkeeping, petition approval standards, and detailed ANDA content (labeling, bioequivalence, CMC, patent certifications, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: ACNU failure report content
rubrics_metrics.description: Report must include the following information, if known: drug product strength; National Drug Code (NDC); lot number; NDA or ANDA number; initial reporter information (name, address, telephone); unique case identification number (same across initial and follow-up reports); ACNU failure term(s); date of ACNU failure (or best estimate); date the ACNU failure was reported to the applicant; location of the ACNU failure (including business name and contact information); concise narrative summary of the ACNU failure (including whether the consumer accessed/used the product without successfully fulfilling ACNU; successfully fulfilled ACNU but could not access/use the product; or was unable to attempt to fulfill the ACNU); description of remedial action initiated or completed (examples: repair, replace, recall, inspection, modification, adjustment); and description of corrective action to prevent reoccurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes explicit items (i)–(x). The narrative summary must indicate which of the listed circumstances occurred. Remedial actions should be described including type; corrective actions should describe prevention of recurrence. "If available to the applicant" qualifier applies to the information.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACNU failure report submission timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must submit the report of an ACNU failure as soon as possible but no later than 15 calendar days from the date when the applicant has acquired the minimum dataset for an ACNU failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must investigate new information about a previously submitted report and submit any follow-up report as soon as possible but no later than 15 calendar days after obtaining the new information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic format for ACNU failure submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The report of an ACNU failure must be submitted to FDA in accordance with § 314.80(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant may request in writing a waiver of the electronic submission requirement under paragraph (b)(3)(v)(F)(1) of this section in accordance with § 314.90 or § 314.99.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACNU failure recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must maintain records of all reports of ACNU failures and associated adverse drug experiences known to the applicant for a period of 10 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records must include raw data and any correspondence relating to a report of an ACNU failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-application reporting rule
rubrics_metrics.description: For all reports required by this section, information common to more than one application shall be submitted only to the application first approved and shall not be reported separately on each application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submission must identify all applications to which the report applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient identification and privacy in reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should not include names and addresses of individual patients in reports; applicants should code patient names whenever possible and retain the code in their files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must maintain sufficient patient identification information to permit FDA, alone or with investigator records, to identify the name and address of individual patients when the agency needs to investigate further or believes the reports may not represent actual results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of approval for failure to report
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant fails to make reports required under this section, FDA may withdraw approval of the application and prohibit continued marketing of the drug product that is the subject of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply with reporting obligations carries the regulatory consequence of possible withdrawal of approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver request content (§ 314.90(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A waiver request must be submitted with supporting documentation in an NDA or in an amendment or supplement to an NDA and must contain one of: (1) an explanation why compliance with the requirement is unnecessary or cannot be achieved; (2) a description of an alternative submission that satisfies the purpose of the requirement; or (3) other information justifying a waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver requests must be made under this section for requirements applying under §§ 314.50 through 314.81 and certain study-criteria under § 314.126(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver grant criteria (§ 314.90(b)–(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may grant a waiver if it finds: (1) the applicant's compliance is unnecessary for evaluation or cannot be achieved; (2) the applicant's alternative submission satisfies the requirement; or (3) the applicant's submission otherwise justifies a waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If FDA grants a waiver for a requirement under §§ 314.50–314.81, the waived requirement will not constitute a basis for refusal to approve an NDA under § 314.125.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for abbreviated applications (§ 314.92)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviated applications (ANDAs) are suitable for drug products that are the same as a listed drug (identical in active ingredient(s), dosage form, strength, route of administration, and conditions of use, with certain exceptions for exclusivity/patent-protected uses), and for products declared suitable by FDA through petition procedures (§ 10.30) and § 314.93.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a listed drug has been voluntarily withdrawn or not offered for sale, an ANDA sponsor must comply with § 314.122. FDA will publish a list of listed drugs for which ANDAs may be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to request change from a listed drug (§ 314.93) — scope and filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions are only accepted for the specific changes described in paragraph (b) of § 314.93. A person who wants to submit an ANDA for a drug not identical to a listed drug in route, dosage form, strength, or with a substituted active ingredient must first obtain permission from FDA via petition in accordance with § 10.20 and the format in § 10.30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must contain the information specified in § 10.30 and any additional information required by § 314.93; if inconsistent provisions exist, the provisions of § 314.93 apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition content requirements (§ 314.93(d)–(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must identify the listed drug, include a copy of proposed labeling and approved labeling, and show that (1) active ingredients of the proposed product are of the same pharmacological or therapeutic class as the reference listed drug; and (2) the drug can be expected to have the same therapeutic effect for each condition of use sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For combination products with one different active ingredient, the petitioner must show the different ingredient has previously been approved in a listed drug or is not a 'new drug' under section 201(p). FDA will approve or disapprove the petition within 90 days unless specific findings require investigations or otherwise justify disapproval (detailed grounds listed in § 314.93(e)(1)(i)–(vi)). If FDA approves a petition, its response may describe additional information required to support an ANDA; FDA may request additional information at any time during ANDA review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition withdrawal and post-approval limits (§ 314.93(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA may withdraw approval of a petition if new information demonstrates the petition no longer satisfies approval conditions. If, after petition approval but before approval of an ANDA under the petition, an NDA is approved covering the change, the petition/listed drug can no longer serve as the basis for ANDA submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person seeking approval for such a drug must submit a new ANDA identifying a pharmaceutically equivalent reference listed drug and comply with applicable regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: ANDA submission copies and FDA guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Three copies of the ANDA are required: an archival copy, a review copy, and a field copy. FDA will maintain guidance documents on the format and content of ANDAs to assist applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow the form and content required under § 314.94 and may consult FDA guidance for formatting details.

rubrics_metrics.name: ANDA application form requirement (§ 314.94(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must submit a completed and signed application form that contains the information described under § 314.50(a)(1), (a)(3), (a)(4), and (a)(5). The applicant must state whether the submission is an ANDA under this section or a supplement to an ANDA under § 314.97.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all referenced § 314.50(a) items are completed and the submission status clearly stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: ANDA table of contents (§ 314.94(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The archival copy of the ANDA must contain a table of contents that shows the volume number and page number of the contents of the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table of contents should allow reviewers to locate materials by volume and page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for ANDA submission (§ 314.94(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: An ANDA must refer to a listed drug (ordinarily the drug chosen as the reference standard for bioequivalence testing). The ANDA must contain the name of the reference listed drug (including dosage form and strength), a statement about whether the reference listed drug is entitled to marketing exclusivity under section 505(j)(5)(F), and, if based on an approved petition under § 10.30 and § 314.93, the FDA-assigned docket number and a copy of FDA's correspondence approving the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The basis information ties the ANDA to a specific reference listed drug and documents any petition reliance or exclusivity considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions of use (§ 314.94(a)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement that the conditions of use prescribed, recommended, or suggested in the proposed labeling have been previously approved for the reference listed drug, and a reference to the applicant's annotated proposed labeling and to the currently approved labeling for the reference listed drug.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must annotate proposed labeling and cross-reference approved labeling to demonstrate identical conditions of use (except for allowable petition-authorized differences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Active ingredient equivalence (§ 314.94(a)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: For single-active-ingredient products: a statement that the active ingredient of the proposed product is the same as that of the reference single-active-ingredient listed drug plus references to annotated labeling. For combination products: information to show that active ingredients are the same as those of the reference listed drug except for any different active ingredient that has been the subject of an approved petition, including information to show the different active ingredient is itself an active ingredient of another listed drug or not a 'new drug.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include statements and labeling cross-references; for differing active ingredients under approved petition include any additional FDA-required information about the different ingredient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Route of administration, dosage form, and strength equivalence (§ 314.94(a)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Information to show that the route of administration, dosage form, and strength of the proposed product are the same as those of the reference listed drug, except for differences approved under a petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a statement of sameness and references to annotated proposed and approved labeling; if differences are petition-approved, submit any information FDA may require about the differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bioequivalence information and study reports (§ 314.94(a)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Information that shows the drug product is bioequivalent to the reference listed drug. A complete study report must be submitted for the bioequivalence study relied upon for approval; for other bioequivalence studies on the same formulation, submit either a complete or summary report. For ANDAs based on an approved petition, submit results of any bioavailability/bioequivalence testing required by the Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If summary reports are submitted and FDA has concerns, FDA may require a complete report. For proposed products with a different active ingredient, FDA requires demonstration (A) adequate scientific basis that substitution yields safety/effectiveness not adversely affected; (B) unchanged active ingredients are bioequivalent to reference; and (C) different active ingredient is bioequivalent to an approved dosage form for same indication or to a product not meeting 'new drug' definition. For each in vivo/in vitro study include (A) description of analytical and statistical methods; and (B) for human studies a statement regarding IRB compliance or applicability of §§ 56.104/56.105 and compliance with informed consent regulations in part 50.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling requirements (§ 314.94(a)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide copy of currently approved labeling for the listed drug (including Medication Guide if applicable); copies of proposed labeling (4 copies draft or 12 copies final printed); a statement that proposed labeling is the same as the reference labeling except for annotated/explained differences; and a side-by-side comparison of proposed labeling with approved labeling with all differences annotated and explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labeling must be the same as the reference labeling except for changes required by petition approval, manufacturer differences, differences in expiration date, formulation, bioavailability, pharmacokinetics, or labeling updated to comply with current FDA guidance, or omission of indication protected by patent/exclusivity. Include container label, package insert, and Medication Guide as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemistry, manufacturing, and controls (CMC) (§ 314.94(a)(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the information required under § 314.50(d)(1), including proposed or actual master production record (with equipment description) to be used for manufacture of a commercial lot. Identify and characterize inactive ingredients and provide information demonstrating they do not affect safety or efficacy, with special rules for parenteral, ophthalmic/otic, and topical/ aerosol/ nasal products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally parenteral products must have same inactive ingredients and concentrations as the reference listed drug, except limited changes (preservative, buffer, antioxidant) may be permitted with demonstration they do not affect safety or efficacy; ophthalmic/otic products generally must match but limited permitted differences exist (preservative, buffer, tonicity adjuster, thickening agent) with demonstration of non-impact—note prohibition in ophthalmic products against changing buffer/tonicity for the purpose of claiming therapeutic advantage; topical/aerosol/nasal products generally must contain the same inactive ingredients but an ANDA may include different inactive ingredients if characterized and demonstrated to not affect safety/efficacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Samples (§ 314.94(a)(10))
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the information required under § 314.50(e)(1) and (e)(2)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Samples need not be submitted until requested by FDA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other information (§ 314.94(a)(11))
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the information required under § 314.50(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catch-all for additional information required by cross-reference to § 314.50(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent certification and associated statements (§ 314.94(a)(12))
rubrics_metrics.description: For patents claiming drug substance, product, or method of use that in the applicant's opinion claim the reference listed drug or a use being sought, provide an appropriate patent certification or statement for each such patent (Paragraph I–IV certifications): Paragraph I (patent information not submitted); Paragraph II (patent expired); Paragraph III (date patent will expire); Paragraph IV (patent is invalid, unenforceable, or will not be infringed — must be in specified form and accompanied by statement of compliance with § 314.95 notice/ timing/content requirements). Also include patent certifications/statements for patents covering the first-approved patented drug if ANDA refers to a listed drug that is a licensed generic. If no relevant patents, provide a certification stating there are no such patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special rules cover method-of-use patents (statements explaining that method-of-use patent does not claim a proposed indication or applicable certification if labeling includes an indication that may be claimed), licensing agreements (para IV cert plus statement that applicant has been granted a patent license and any consent-to-approval letter), untimely filing of patent information (rules about applicants who submitted ANDA before late-listed patent info), disputed patent information (procedures to seek confirmation under § 314.53(f)), and amended certifications. Amended certification rules include obligations after finding of infringement, after request to remove patent info from list, and other amendments when certifications are no longer accurate; timing and content rules for amendments are specified (including when an amendment is not required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial certification or disclosure statement (§ 314.94(a)(13))
rubrics_metrics.description: An ANDA must contain a financial certification or disclosure statement as required by part 54 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with the form and content requirements of part 54 regarding payments, interests, or other financial disclosures relevant to clinical investigators.
